title: The Motional Emf Bench
summary: Find the emf of falling wires, loops leaving a field, spinning rods and wheels, with polarity.
subject: physics
learningOutcome: The student can find the motional emf of a moving wire and its polarity, the emf and duration for a loop leaving a field, and the emf of a rotating rod or wheel.

levels.title: A falling wire
levels.adds: Baseline: ε = Blv, with the polarity from the force q v × B on positive charge (Ex 6.6).
hints: ε = B l v, with B in tesla.
Find the direction of v × B: that is the way positive charge is pushed.
The end the positive charge is pushed towards is at the higher potential.

levels.title: A loop leaving the field
levels.adds: New idea: only the edge parallel to the boundary cuts field lines, and the emf lasts while the loop leaves (Ex 6.4).
hints: Decide which edge is parallel to the boundary: it is perpendicular to the motion.
ε = B l v for that edge, with lengths in metres.
The time is the distance the loop must travel divided by the speed.

levels.title: A spinning rod
levels.adds: New idea: the speed along a rotating rod rises from zero, so ε = ½Bωl² (Ex 6.5, Example 6.6).
hints: ω must be in rad/s: multiply revolutions per second by 2π.
The two ends of the rod are the two terminals.

levels.title: The wheel
levels.adds: More steps: spokes in parallel do not add, and the units need converting (Example 6.7).
hints: Each spoke is a rotating rod: ½Bωl².
All the spokes join the same axle and rim, so they are in parallel.
Convert rev/min to rad/s and gauss to tesla.

misconceptions: The emf of a rotating rod is Blωl, using the speed of the tip
Each extra spoke adds its emf
A loop wholly inside a uniform field has an emf as it moves
